title: AcmeCorp POC — Week 4 Touchpoint: Infra Access & Latency Deep-dive
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on environment readiness and an initial interpretation of staging benchmarks. Customer still needs subnet routing updates and a KMS key policy tweak. Redwood SE walked through KV-cache effects on tail latency and recommended batching/quant profiles. Agreed action items: provide precise curl examples, update gateway auth, schedule a short latency focused run with controlled steady-state traffic.
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-08-25
- Start: 15:30 PT
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE); Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE); Daniel Wu (Redwood SE); Michael Stone (Acme Eng Mgr); Sara Lin (Acme Infra Lead); Tara Gomez (Acme Security); Jon Park (Acme SRE)

[00:00] Alex Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 45 minute-ish sync, we have a few items — access, a quick bench read, and security Qs. Priya you good to lead the bench part?
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Yep, thanks Alex. Quick agenda check, I have the sampler results from yesterday's staging run, also want to call out one weirdness on K V cache hits -- I'm seeing a tail p99 spike when cache cold-starts, so plan to explain that and suggested mitigations.
[00:28] Michael Stone: Cool. Also just flag, Sara is on the call for network updates and Tara for KMS and audit concerns. We still don't have cross-account KMS policy applied so we couldn't test the private deployment path yet.
[00:42] Sara Lin: Correct, we opened a ticket with infra but the route table change hasn't propagated to the staging subnet. Hoping to get that by end of day Friday.
[00:50] Alex Reed: Ok we'll note that as blocker for the private flow. For hosted API you can proceed, but dedicated/Private requires that route and the K M S key permission.
[01:05] Priya Kapoor: Jumping into the numbers — yesterday's run: steady-state QPS ~40, token lengths median ~90, we saw p50 around 85ms, p95 about 210ms, p99 around 520ms with the cold-start windows. I put a short slide in the meeting notes link.
[01:25] Michael Stone: Hmm p99 520ms is higher than we expected. Our SLA target is p95 < 250ms and p99 < 400ms. Is that before or after prefix caching?
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: That was with only partial prefix caching — about 60% hit rate. When we simulate warmed cache at 95% the p99 drops to ~320ms. The main tail is from KV lookup misses and the longer model kernel path on the first few tokens. Also we noticed batching helps overall throughput but can increase tail slightly for single-request latency.
[02:05] Jon Park: Can you remind us what you mean by KV? Is that the local key-value store for cached past tokens?
[02:12] Priya Kapoor: Yeah sorry — K V cache, the attention key/value cache for transformer decoders, saved between steps. If it's cold we need to populate it which adds CPU/GPU overhead per request.
[02:25] Daniel Wu: Also worth calling out the runtime chooses different kernels for longer or shorter sequences; that variance shows up in p99 if your traffic has a long-tail of longer contexts.
[02:38] Sara Lin: On the network side, we saw a spike in egress queueing when multiple clients retried during the run. We are planning to enable sticky sessions at the gateway to keep cache affinity. Any advice?
[02:52] Priya Kapoor: Sticky sessions help, yes. For enterprise pods we also recommend token-based affinity or edge-side caching. There is a tradeoff — affinity improves cold-hit ratio but reduces overall load balancing flexibility.
[03:10] Alex Reed: For your use-case, where most calls are high QPS with similar prompt prefixes, affinity probably helps. We'll give a recommended config.
[03:22] Michael Stone: Security: Tara, do you have the KMS question?
[03:27] Tara Gomez: Yeah. We attempted to grant Redwood's service principal the decrypt permission but saml/user mapping got weird and the key policy rejects the cross-account principal. We need instructions for the exact IAM statement and what the Redwood side expects.
[03:44] Alex Reed: We'll provide a minimal key policy snippet and a template trust relationship. I'll also loop in our security engineer with a short example. We'll put it in the shared doc.
[03:55] Priya Kapoor: Back to benches — I also ran a quick experiment with 8-bit quant on the model; quality delta looks negligible for your prompt set but latency improved ~12% at p95. We can provide quant profiles if you want to keep quality locked.
[04:15] Michael Stone: That's interesting. Are there fallbacks if quant causes failure modes?
[04:21] Daniel Wu: Yes, Redwood supports rollouts and automatic fallback to float16 or full precision when quality regressions are detected. Also you can pin model versions per route.
[04:33] Jon Park: Great. Can we schedule a controlled run that reproduces the p99 spike? We want to capture tracing and flame graphs.
[04:40] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely. Suggestion: run a 30-minute steady-state with gradually increasing QPS and a warm-up phase; we'll collect traces and provide backend kernel selection logs. We can also enable debug-level traces for two runs.
[05:00] Sara Lin: One more infra item: current NAT gateway concurrency limit on our account is 100 concurrent connections; will that be a bottleneck?
[05:08] Alex Reed: Possibly during bursts. We recommended using regional egress points or increasing the NAT capacity for the test. Also consider the dedicated path which avoids multi-tenant egress.
[05:20] Michael Stone: On dedicated vs hosted — we like hosted for speed but worried about PII; is there an option to get logging turned off or mask tokens?
[05:30] Priya Kapoor: We offer token-level masking and retention rules; for enterprise customers we provide Private with customer-controlled KMS which keeps keys in your account. For hosted we can set retention to zero and disable conversation logs for specific routes.
[05:48] Tara Gomez: We need SOC 2 and ISO docs. Do you have a current SOC 2 Type II report?
[05:54] Alex Reed: Yes, linking it in the notes. We'll send the summary and the full compliance pack via secure link.
[06:05] Daniel Wu: Quick demo of the trace snippet — (screen share described) — see here, the kernel handoff is at ~48ms for short contexts, the heavy tail appears when we hit the slower attention kernel.
[06:25] Michael Stone: Is there a config we can tweak to avoid that kernel?
[06:28] Daniel Wu: You can set a max-context hint or pad inputs to a stable token length, also quant and compiler flags may select a different kernel. We'll provide recommended compiler flags for your model.
[06:42] Alex Reed: Let's take a few clarifying questions from the team.
[06:48] Sara Lin: What's the recommended batch size for 40 QPS?
[06:52] Priya Kapoor: At 40 QPS and median tokens ~90, we saw best throughput with micro-batching of 4-8. End-to-end latency tradeoff was minimal until batch sizes hit 16.
[07:06] Jon Park: Can we get the exact curl examples to reproduce the staging runs (headers, auth flow)?
[07:10] Alex Reed: Yes, we'll post curl + python examples.
[07:14] Tara Gomez: Also need a step-by-step for SSO and provisioning service principal. We had some mismatch on SAML assertions previously.
[07:21] Alex Reed: Noted. We'll include a SAML troubleshooting checklist.
[07:28] Michael Stone: One odd line in your run, Priya — you mentioned a 60% prefix hit rate. Is that something we can improve with a short-term change?
[07:36] Priya Kapoor: Yes, improving affinity and pre-warming common prefixes reduces misses. Also consider moving high-frequency prompts to a cached route or using the built-in prompt cache.
[07:50] Daniel Wu: We're also going to test an intermediate change: increasing session affinity TTL to 20 minutes to keep cache hot during bursts.
[08:00] Alex Reed: Ok, let's capture the blockers — (1) route table propagation, (2) KMS policy update, (3) NAT concurrency question. Anything else?
[08:08] Michael Stone: I'd add 'curl examples & run recipe' and 'schedule focused p99 run with traces'
[08:15] Alex Reed: Good. We'll recap next steps and action items.
[08:22] Priya Kapoor: Quick note: we put a deck and the raw measurements in the shared folder: https://redwood.app/shared/acme/poc-week4-deck and the bench CSV: https://redwood.app/shared/acme/poc-week4-bench.csv
[08:40] Tara Gomez: Thanks, that's helpful.
[08:45] Alex Reed: All right, we'll reconvene next week same time unless you want earlier. Any objections?
[08:51] Michael Stone: No, same time works.
[08:54] Alex Reed: Great, thanks everyone.

End of recording.
